designBreaks.attack: Bypass of R1's goal 'interrupted' fence (skip while latest receipt disposition is stop|pause AND receipt.objectiveRevisionAfter === domain.revision). Revision movers that are not user goal mutations lift it.
designBreaks.bypassOrRegression: (1) Attach replacement bumps the revision to max(live+1, persisted) (src/objective/authority.ts:865-866). The web daemon calls it on every thread hydrate, keyed to the same live session id (src/apps/web-daemon/server.ts:440-444), and the web wake re-arms on attach and on any revision change (src/apps/web-daemon/goal-wake-compose.ts:170-177). So reopening a thread re-arms an auth-stopped goal. (2) A continuation or model actor setNextActions is allowed by policy (src/objective/policy.ts setNextActions row) and bumps the revision. (3) The operator read /goal and GET /readout/goal runs reconcile first (src/objective/freshness.ts:34-48; src/apps/cli/slash/objective.ts:126; src/apps/web-daemon/readout-compose.ts:68). That can commit invalidateVerification (src/host/runtime/objective-verifier-wire.ts:655), so just viewing the goal can lift the fence (static for this third path). R1's T2 tests only a user mutation lifting the fence, so it stays green.
designBreaks.evidence: Probe pa-fence-and-blockers.ts output: `1a before-attach {receiptRevAfter:2, domainRev:2, fenceHolds:true}`, then `1a after-attach {attach:{ok:true,revision:3}, receiptRevAfter:2, domainRev:3, fenceHolds:false}`; `1b continuation setNextActions {ok:true, domainRev:3, fenceHolds:false}`.

designBreaks.attack: Reuse check: does a typed 'goal stopped with a cause, operator clears it' model already exist?
designBreaks.bypassOrRegression: Yes, and R1 missed it. Objective Blocker {reason, waitingOn, dependencyId} derives status 'blocked' (src/objective/types.ts:36-60, :111-118). Wake then skips 'not-active' (src/objective/goal-wake-policy.ts:143). BlockerObservation already provides host-attributed hysteresis: 3 distinct attemptIds per dependencyId promote to a single blocker, deduped (src/objective/core-store/criteria-ops.ts:24-76), and observations are cleared on progress (src/objective/blocker-observation.ts:62-72). Rendering and clearing exist on both surfaces: the CLI prints 'blockers (/goal unblock to clear)' and 'observing N/3' (src/apps/cli/slash/goal-render.ts:84,142), and the web sends clearBlocker (apps/web-frontend/src/components/slash-goal.ts:326). The model cannot clear a blocker. R1's `interruption` receipt field, the interrupted/failure-streak skips, GOAL_FAILURE_STREAK_CAP=3, the new receipt schema migration and the revision fence together form a parallel model of the same fact, and the fence is the bypassable part. The structural alternative: settlement, as the system actor, adds a blocker keyed by dependencyId=reasonCode for stop/pause dispositions, and observes one for retry dispositions. That needs no schema migration and no new skip reason.
designBreaks.evidence: Probe pa part 2: `system addBlocker {ok:true, status:"blocked", decision:{skip:"not-active"}}`; `model clearBlocker {ok:false, reason:"actor-forbidden"}`; `user clearBlocker {ok:true, status:"active", decision:{delayMs:30000}}`. Probe pb: user setExplicitStatus on an active goal bumps revision 2→3.

designBreaks.attack: BUG-4 inline `turn.run{input}` reuses startTurn, which never writes draftInput. The unchanged pause recorder keys a turn.run's paused prompt off state.draftInput.
designBreaks.bypassOrRegression: pausedTurnOf special-cases only turn.submit (src/kernel/session/scheduler-turn-terminals.ts:131-147). A turn started from inline input that pauses for approval therefore records prompt "". The post-approval resume, whether a client turn.run or the daemon's serverAutoContinues continuation (src/apps/web-daemon/server/approval-continuation.ts:84-86), sends an empty prompt. The host always appends a user text block from the prompt (src/host/runtime/internal/context-binding/turn-runner.ts:271-277), so approved work resumes without the user's message. That an empty text block also makes providers 400 is UNVERIFIED. R1's W4 says 'the paused-turn resume path is unchanged', but it has no inline-input+approval case.
designBreaks.evidence: Probe pc-inline-input-pause.ts, real onApprovalRequested + real approval.respond + real bare turn.run: `A inline-input state (draftInput empty) {pausedPrompt:"", resumedHostPrompts:[""]}` vs control `B legacy append+run {pausedPrompt:"deploy it", resumedHostPrompts:["deploy it"]}`.

designBreaks.attack: R1's receipt semantics: generalize sendObjectiveMutation, settle 'rejected' on any matching rejected frame, treat connection-lost as not sent and keep the draft, resend with the same commandId. Tested against the real bridge and engine queue.
designBreaks.bypassOrRegression: Transport commands queue behind the running turn (src/sdk/runtime/session/engine.ts:104-115), and the bridge marks them 'pending' for the whole wait (src/ipc/session/bridge.ts:712-716). A same-id resend gets `rejected duplicate_command` immediately, with nothing to replay, and the turn starts later. sendObjectiveMutation settles 'rejected' on any matching frame (apps/web-frontend/src/ws/session-hooks.ts:1146-1148), so the composer would say 'not sent' for a turn that then runs. A dropped browser socket does not cancel an admitted command either: the turn still runs while the client keeps the draft. Both paths invite a resubmit, which produces a duplicate turn. The honest states are 'accepted-pending' (duplicate_command) and 'outcome unknown' (drop). Codex desktop has exactly that onOutcomeUnknown stage (R1 cited it). R1's option (a) folds both into 'not sent'.
designBreaks.evidence: Probe pf-duplicate-while-queued.ts frame log: [turn.started(A-run), <resend B-run same id>, rejected(B-run,duplicate_command), <release A>, turn.completed(A-run), turn.started(B-run), turn.completed(B-run)]. Probe pg-drop-while-queued.ts: after connected.close()+client.close() the client saw no B frames, yet hostPrompts=["turn A","turn B (queued)"].

designBreaks.attack: R1's new reducer refusal `turn_run_draft_not_empty` combined with the legacy surfaces that still strand drafts.
designBreaks.bypassOrRegression: The non-atomic append+run pair is built in the shared protocol builders and used by the CLI `quanta attach` client (src/apps/cli/attach/commands.ts:54-70, attach-client.ts:338-360), SDK remote handle verbs (src/ipc/session/handle-verbs.ts:39-47) and runtime session verbs (src/sdk/runtime/session.ts:184-187). R1 fixes only the web. No command clears an idle draft: draftInput is written only by append (reducer.ts:73), approval deny (reducer.ts:57) and the turn terminals (scheduler-turn-terminals.ts:300,417,512); turn.cancel on idle and transcript.replace leave it alone (reducer.ts:368-371, :294-299). The web never renders server draftInput (only apps/web-frontend/src/ws/envelope.ts:122 reads it). So one lost run frame from any legacy client or an old tab makes every new web submit fail with an opaque `turn_run_draft_not_empty`, and the web has no escape hatch. The fix belongs in the builder/verb SSOT (one atomic verb for every surface), plus either a visible draft or an explicit clear.
designBreaks.evidence: Static: grep of draftInput writes across src/kernel (listed above); grep of buildInputAppend/buildTurnRun callers. R1's W3 census scans only apps/web-frontend.

missedHoles.what: The OpenAI Responses SSE `type:"error"` event (typed ResponseErrorEvent {code,message}) has no dispatcher arm and is silently skipped. Without prior content the stream becomes a synthetic `rate_limit` 'likely transport throttle', so a quota error is retried as a throttle. With prior content the turn COMPLETES successfully with a truncated answer and the provider failure is invisible. This is the default BYOK surface, and chatgpt-oauth reuses streamResponsesSurface. The structural fix is an exhaustive Record over the SDK's ResponseStreamEvent['type'] with explicit ignore rows, not an if-chain that falls through to 'continue'.

overEngineeringOrHeuristics: The receipt `interruption` field, the `interrupted` and `failure-streak` skips, GOAL_FAILURE_STREAK_CAP=3, the zod migration and the revision fence are a parallel model of the existing Blocker/BlockerObservation machinery. That machinery already derives 'blocked', dedupes per dependencyId, promotes at 3 distinct attempts, clears on progress, persists, renders on CLI and web, and can be cleared only by the user (src/objective/types.ts:111-126, core-store/criteria-ops.ts:24-76, blocker-observation.ts:62-72, goal-render.ts:84).

The two-hop projection LLMErrorKind → StopReasonCode → GoalWakeDisposition sits beside four more per-vendor tables (Anthropic type, OpenAI code, ResponseError code, STATUS_KIND) and the surviving classifyBadRequest code/marker rules, one of which conflicts with R1's permission_error row.
